title: Quotients by smooth unipotent subgroups embed into affine space
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $U\subseteq G$ be a smooth closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Assume that $U$ is unipotent in this explicit sense: for some $m\geq1$ there is a homomorphism $\rho:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] that is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and every $u\in U(k)$ satisfies $(\rho(u)-I_m)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Let $G/U$ be the separated finite-type scheme representing the fppf coset sheaf of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. Then there exist $n\geq0$ and a $k$-morphism $j:G/U\to\mathbf A^n_k$, where $\mathbf A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that is an immersion: $j$ factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $\mathbf A^n_k$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. No normality or connectedness assumption on $U$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286 (PDF p.298); Corollaries 14.6 and 14.12, printed pp.282--283, identify unipotence with the stated faithful matrix condition for smooth groups.

proof.text: By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the supplied closed immersion $\rho$, $U$ is affine and its coordinate ring is a quotient of $k[x_{ij},D^{-1}]$, the coordinate ring of $\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ in [def-sc-general-linear-group]. The images of the finitely many $x_{ij}$ and $D^{-1}$ generate that quotient, so the one affine chart of $U$ makes $U$ finite type over $k$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The surjective coordinate map of $\rho$ also makes $\rho(A)$ injective for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$: two algebra maps out of a quotient agreeing on the original ring agree on every residue class.

source.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286; explicit verification of its affine finite-type subgroup input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] to $U$ and $\rho$. Smoothness is assumed, affineness, finite type and faithfulness were verified in Step 1, and we can take $\bar k=k$ because $k$ is algebraically closed. The given nilpotence condition is therefore exactly its geometric-point hypothesis. Obtain a closed embedding of $U$ into an upper unitriangular group. Thus $U$ satisfies the unipotence convention of [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial].

source.place: Corollaries 14.6 and 14.12, printed pp.282--283; Proposition 14.26, p.286.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] with $H=U$. It gives a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $G$-representation $V$ and a line $L$ whose stabilizer on every algebra is $U$. Restriction to $L$ defines a character $\chi:U\to\mathbf G_m$: in a basis starting with a generator of $L$, the first column of the restricted matrix is $(a,0,\ldots,0)$; its inverse gives $a\in A^\times$, and multiplication multiplies these scalars. The coefficient $a$ is regular on $U$, so this is a group-scheme homomorphism. By [def-sc-gm-ga], $\mathbf G_m$ is itself a one-fold product of multiplicative groups, hence is of multiplicative type. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], $\chi_A(u)=1$ for every $A$ and $u\in U(A)$. Consequently $U$ fixes $L$ pointwise after every algebra extension. This proves $L\subseteq V^U$; the stronger equality printed in Proposition 14.26 is unnecessary.

source.place: Theorem 4.27 and Remark 4.30, printed pp.94--96; Corollary 14.18(a), p.284; Proposition 14.26, p.286 (only inclusion of the line in the fixed space is needed).

proof.text: Choose $0\ne x\in L$. For any commutative $k$-algebra $A$, $x_A$ is a basis of the free rank-one summand $L_A$. If $g\in G(A)$ fixes $x_A$, then it preserves $L_A$, so the all-algebra stabilizer equality of [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] gives $g\in U(A)$. Conversely each $u\in U(A)$ fixes $x_A$ by Step 3. This includes the zero algebra, where all point sets are singletons. These equalities are natural in $A$, and hence identify the scheme-theoretic vector stabilizer $G_x$ with $U$.

source.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286, last sentence; Remark 4.30, printed p.96, for stabilizers on every algebra.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $V$, put $n=\dim_k V\geq1$, and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. The representation gives a scheme action on $X$: if $(r_{ij})$ is its matrix of regular functions on $G$, the coordinate pullback of the action sends $t_i$ to $\sum_j r_{ij}\otimes t_j$. The matrix multiplication and identity equations give the two action equations. The $t_i$ generate the coordinate algebra, so $X$ is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Thus $X$ satisfies the target hypotheses of the orbit statements below, with $x$ as a $k$-point.

source.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286: regard the representation as an action on the affine space underlying V, with its coordinate action made explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry], the reduced orbit $O_x$ is a locally closed subscheme of $X$. Here $k$ is algebraically closed and $G$ is smooth, connected, affine and finite type, exactly as required. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], the map $gG_x\mapsto gx$ is an isomorphism $G/G_x\simeq O_x$. Step 4 gives $G_x=U$, so it identifies the specified fppf quotient $G/U$ with $O_x$. Compose this isomorphism with the locally closed inclusion $O_x\hookrightarrow X=\mathbf A^n_k$. A locally closed subscheme is a closed subscheme of an open subscheme, which is precisely the immersion convention of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This gives the required $j$ and $n\geq0$.

source.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286; Propositions 7.11--7.12 and 7.17, printed pp.141--143.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 14.26, printed p.286, expanded using Theorem 4.27, Remark 4.30, Corollaries 14.12 and 14.18(a), and Propositions 7.11--7.17. Only L contained in V^U is used, correcting the unnecessary equality printed in the proof.

Step 2: every hypothesis of lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding holds with k̄=k, and its output is the unipotence definition of lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial. Step 3: the Chevalley stabilizer of L on all algebras gives a regular character χ:U→G_m by Yoneda; G_m is of multiplicative type with r=1, so χ=1, which proves only L⊆V^U and that is enough. Step 4: G_x=U as subfunctors, an elementary step. Step 5: the linear action on A^n is of finite type and separated by the Mathlib leaf affine source⇒separated. Step 6: the hypotheses of the orbit-geometry and orbit-quotient nodes match exactly, both define G_x by the same formula, and a locally closed subscheme gives the immersion of def-weil-closed-immersion. Edge cases U=1, U=G, unipotent U⊂SL_2 (not closed) and disconnected Z/p are all fine. lean.statement: theorem exists_unipotent_homogeneous_quotient_immersion {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G U : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj U] [IsAffine G.left] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (i : U ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] [Smooth U.hom] (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (ρ : U ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) k) [IsMonHom ρ] [IsClosedImmersion ρ.left] (hρ : ∀ a : (Spec (.of k)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ U, ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ((GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) k k (a ≫ ρ) : Matrix (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} m) k) - 1) ^ N = 0) (Q : Over (Spec (.of k))) (q : G ⟶ Q) [IsSeparated Q.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Q.hom] [QuasiCompact Q.hom] (hQ : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (yoneda.obj Q)) (ηq : coequalizer (yoneda.map (fst G U)) (yoneda.map (lift (fst G U) (snd G U ≫ i) ≫ μ[G])) ⟶ yoneda.obj Q) (hηq : coequalizer.π _ _ ≫ ηq = yoneda.map q) (hquot : ∀ Z : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun f : yoneda.obj Q ⟶ Z.obj ↦ ηq ≫ f)) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (j : Q ⟶ (Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))).asOver (Spec (.of k))), IsImmersion j.left
lean.note: Uses the existing GL scheme and homMulEquiv, and exactly the fppf coset sheafification interface recorded by lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry. The target is literally Spec of the polynomial k-algebra in Fin n. IsImmersion is equivalent to closed-then-open factorization; no normality or connectedness of U is assumed.
